variables.claim_asserts: At fixed length, plaice lose weight from roughly November to March or April and regain it by November, wholly because of spawning and subsequent rebuilding.
variables.test_measures: Length- and sex-adjusted trends in log10 Fulton K by day within Q1 and Q3, maturity-stage contrasts, and the ratio of the Q1 decline in immature versus mature North Sea plaice.

modality.note: Individual length, weight, haul date, sex, and maturity stage from NS-IBTS directly support fixed-length seasonal condition comparisons and a nonspawning immature control.

assumptions.note: Immature fish are a valid negative control for a mechanism claimed to depend wholly on spawning. Calendar date is partly confounded with survey geography and haul clustering is ignored, but mature and immature fish share the survey design and the conclusion rests on their comparative slopes.

scope.claim_scope: Plaice and similar seasonally spawning fishes over the November-to-April loss and May-to-November recovery cycle.
scope.test_scope: Modern North Sea plaice sampled during NS-IBTS Q1 (January-early March) and Q3 (July-September), 2015-2024.

reasons: The analysis measures the claimed fixed-length quantity through log10 K = log10(100W/L^3), adjusting for 1-cm length class and sex.
P1 and P2 test the predicted seasonal directions, while the spent-versus-maturing contrast directly tests weight loss associated with spawning.
The refutation of 'wholly' uses the pre-declared immature control: immature Q1 decline is -5.67% per 30 days versus -4.44% in mature fish, a slope ratio of 1.285.

The interpretation clearly states that Q1 and Q3 do not cover Thompson's full November-April and May-November intervals, so the verdict is faithful only to the sampled seasonal windows and modern North Sea population.
what_would_change_it: Add monthly fixed-length plaice observations spanning November through the following November at a consistent locality, with maturity stage, gonad mass, somatic reserves, feeding, temperature, and haul-level or site-level controls.
